items.entity: Load on the face opposite the fixed face (configuration 1)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says the loads are 'applied to the side opposite to a fixed one' and points to the figure (Fig. 2(A), cited as 'Fig.1(A, D)'). Where on that face the configuration-1 load acts is never stated. Positions below are fractions (y, z) of the loaded face, with xz the symmetry plane named in the Fig. 3 caption.
readings: Centre of the loaded face: (y, z) = (0.5, 0.5)
Midpoint of the bottom edge of the loaded face: (y, z) = (0.5, 0)
Midpoint of the top edge of the loaded face: (y, z) = (0.5, 1)
Off the mid-plane, e.g. at a bottom corner of the loaded face: (y, z) = (0 or 1, 0)

items.entity: Load on the face opposite the fixed face (configuration 1)
items.description: The text never says whether configuration 1 is a concentrated force, a line load or a distributed traction, or how large the loaded patch is. The BEM uses piecewise-constant tractions on boundary triangles (Sec. 2.2), so even a 'point' load covers an unspecified number of voxel faces. Only Fig. 2(A) shows it.
readings: Concentrated force at a single point/node
Uniform traction on a single voxel face (1/64 x 1/64 patch)
Uniform traction on a small square patch of several voxel faces (e.g. 4x4 voxels = 1/16 x 1/16)
Line load across the full width of the face (along an edge or the mid-height line)
Uniform traction over the entire face

items.entity: Load on the face opposite the fixed face (configuration 1)
items.description: The load direction is never stated. The word 'cantilever' and the xz 'symmetry plane' cross-section in the Fig. 3 caption suggest a transverse load lying in the xz plane, but the direction is only shown in Fig. 2(A). The axes below assume the fixed face is x=0 and the loaded face is x=1.
readings: Transverse, parallel to the loaded face and lying in the xz symmetry plane (+/-z)
Transverse, perpendicular to the xz plane (+/-y)
Normal to the loaded face, i.e. axial tension/compression (+/-x)

items.entity: Load on the face opposite the fixed face (configuration 1)
items.description: No force or traction value is given for this example. Sec. 4.1 and Fig. 2(F) report results only as normalized Psi/Psi0.
readings: Total force F = 1
Unit traction t = 1 on the loaded patch (total force = patch area)

items.entity: Symmetry of configuration 1 (symmetric vs non-symmetric case)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'the symmetric configuration appears significantly stiffer than the non-symmetric one' but does not say which of the two is configuration 1, or which symmetry is meant. The Fig. 3 caption says both examples are cut along an xz 'symmetry plane'.
readings: Configuration 1 is the symmetric case: load symmetric about both mid-planes (e.g. centred on the face)
Configuration 1 is the non-symmetric case, symmetric only about the xz mid-plane (e.g. load at an edge midpoint)
Configuration 1 is the non-symmetric case with no true symmetry plane (load off the xz mid-plane; 'symmetry plane' in Fig. 3 means only the cube's geometric mid-plane)

items.entity: Figure cross-references for the configuration-1 boundary value problem
items.description: Sec. 4.1 cites 'Fig.1(A, D)' for the initial BVPs, plus Fig. 1(B,E), 1(C), 1(F) and Fig. 2(A,B) for results. The captions instead put the cantilever BVPs and results in Fig. 2 and the TD fields in Fig. 3. Read literally, Fig. 1(A) is the Sec. 3 benchmark cube under uniform tension, which would mean a different load.
readings: Intended: configuration 1 is the cantilever BVP of Fig. 2(A) (load not described in text)
Literal: configuration 1 is loaded as in Fig. 1(A), i.e. uniform normal tension over the face opposite the fixed face

items.description: alpha_c = 0.6 is only a stopping threshold: Algorithm 1 (Sec. 2.3) stops once alpha < alpha_c. The design shown is after three hard-kill iterations, so the actual retained fraction is below 0.6 by an overshoot that depends on C and is not reported.
readings: 0.6 exactly
Actual final alpha after the third iteration, somewhat below 0.6 (e.g. about 0.55-0.59)

items.description: Sec. 2.3 gives only a typical range 'C = 0.001÷0.1'. Sec. 4.1 does not give the value used; it only says the level of detail depends on the threshold and that the result comes after three iterations. Sec. 5 says results depend strongly on C. Because the TD is near-singular at a concentrated load, the effective cut-off also depends on how the load is discretized.
readings: C tuned so alpha first falls below 0.6 at the 3rd iteration (on average about 13% of the initial volume removed per iteration)

items.entity: Regularization / filter and material interpolation for a density-based solver
items.description: The paper uses a binary 0/1 hard-kill update with no explicit filter, penalization or move limit; regularization comes only implicitly from C and the voxel size (Sec. 2.3, Sec. 5). No equivalent filter radius or SIMP parameters are given for a density-based, volume-constrained min-compliance solver.
readings: No filter: binary hard-kill (ESO-like) removal using the TD of Eq. (3), 3 iterations
SIMP p = 3 with density/sensitivity filter rmin = 1.5 voxels
SIMP p = 3 with rmin = 2-3 voxels

items.description: Sec. 2.3 and Algorithm 1 apply a 'post-processing procedure excluding isolated voxels and surface irregularities' without defining the connectivity rule or what counts as an irregularity.
readings: Remove only voxel clusters disconnected from the supported body
Also remove voxels with at most one face-connected solid neighbour (spikes / surface irregularities)
No post-processing

items.entity: Voxels under the load and adjacent to the fixed face
items.description: The text does not say whether voxels carrying the load or touching the clamped face are protected from removal. In the hard-kill BEM scheme, removing them would delete that boundary condition, but no non-design region is mentioned in Sec. 2.3 or Sec. 4.1.
readings: No passive region: all 64^3 voxels designable
Voxels under the loaded patch kept solid (non-design)
Loaded voxels plus a one-voxel layer at the fixed face kept solid
